authorization: Owner request 2026-10-13 (Ale): rebuild the grammar classes as live classes; A2 explanations in simple Spanish with occasional English translations. Prototype lesson 230 (Desde, desde hace y hace).

additions.text: Today you will learn to say since when something happens, for how long, and how long ago something happened.
Since when has your head been hurting?
How long have you been working in sales?
And you? How long have you lived here?
We haven’t seen each other in ages!
Say when something that is still true started.
Say how long it has lasted until now.
Place a finished event in the past.
Ask about time.
since
I have lived in Bogotá since 2019.
I have been studying Spanish since March.
I haven’t eaten meat since the summer.
I have been working since eight and haven’t had lunch yet.
Spanish uses the present tense here, where English uses “have lived / have been living”.
for
I have lived in Bogotá for seven years.
I have lived in Bogotá for seven years.
I haven’t seen my family for a month.
desde + a point in time · desde hace + an amount of time
ago
I arrived in Bogotá seven years ago.
I changed jobs two weeks ago.
I called you a little while ago.
I arrived seven years ago.
I have lived there for seven years.
You will often hear “Vivo aquí hace dos años” = I have lived here for two years.
durante = for a finished period
Since when has it been hurting?
Since Saturday. I have barely slept for four days.
Yes, I moved a week ago and carried a lot of boxes.
I have been taking ibuprofen for two days.
I haven’t been to the gym for months.
horario = schedule · desde entonces = since then · tardes libres = free afternoons · todavía = still
